message.text: `StateTree.size` passes every entry of a listing up to 64 MiB to `#sizes`, which asks `git cat-file --batch-check` for every distinct readable blob and keeps the map. It never checks `entryLimit` first. The bound the store's base decision relies on is "Memory for the entries: 65,536 entries, `entryLimit`, checked before any size is read" and "Memory for the sizes: one line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it". The new call bounds those resources only by listing bytes. 64 MiB is a KiB a line only on average: a short record path makes a line about 78 bytes.

evidence.snippet:
| Resource | What bounds it, or who accepted it | Test or issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory for records and cells | 256 MiB of readable blobs at the tip, `tipLimit`, from the sizes git reports, a blob counted at every path it sits at, and the read stops at those sizes. The limit counts bytes, not the heap, which holds each blob several times over, as bytes, text and parsed objects | `store.test.ts`, "the bytes a tip may hold"; [issue #455](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/455) |
| Memory for the entries | 65,536 entries, `entryLimit`, checked before any size is read | `store.test.ts`, "the entries a tip may hold" |
| Memory for the listing of entries | 64 MiB, `listingLimit`, a KiB a line on average; git is stopped there, so the list never grows past it | `store.test.ts`, at the cap and one byte past it |
| A tip past either limit | No write of Melian's makes one: a write measures its commit by both limits before it pushes, and again after it rebuilds on a moved tip, and fails as `unreachable`, pushing nothing, when the commit would pass one. Dispose only shrinks the tip, so it works at either limit. A tip past a limit by another route still fails every call, dispose included. A writer on an older build or a push by hand can make one. A writer clears it by hand, removing files such as a changeset's folder in a commit of their own | `store.test.ts`, "the entries a write may leave" and "the bytes a tip may hold" |
| Memory for the sizes | One line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it | the entry limit's tests |

- A call holds every entry of the tip too, so a tip of more than 65,536 entries, `entryLimit`, fails the call as `unreachable`, naming the branch, the count and the limit, before it reads a size. The listing is bounded first: git is stopped once it prints 64 MiB, `listingLimit`, a KiB a line on average, and the call fails the same way. A write measures the commit it built by both limits before it pushes, and again after it rebuilds on a tip that moved, so no write of Melian's takes the tip past one; a write that would fails as `unreachable` and pushes nothing. Dispose only shrinks the tip, so it works at either limit, and making room before a write is its job. Past a limit, every call but `retire` fails. `retire` reads only the top level of `changesets/` and the folders it was asked to remove, and pushes only a commit that `StateTree.removesOnly` finds removes whole changeset folders and nothing else, by `ls-tree`'s listing of the root and of `changesets/`, so it brings the tip back under; strays still need a writer with git. A retirement removes a folder only while its tree ID is the one its caller saw and its caller names it as merged, and never one that holds a stray or a cell, or whose name `changesets/` lists twice. Merged comes from GitHub's answer for that pull request, never from a record: a closed pull request can reopen at the same head and read a late relay's old round as standing. A cell holds a lease or a disposal mark, and rule 3 of the shared record decision never recreates such a changeset. It judges folders only while their entries and bytes together stay within the limits, and reports the rest as deferred, unread. A new resource a call takes goes in [the decision's table](../decisions/2026-11-14-git-record-store-refuses-by-location.md#what-one-call-uses-and-what-bounds-it), with what bounds it or who accepted it unbounded.

explanation.what: `StateTree.size` passes every entry of a listing up to 64 MiB to `#sizes`, which asks `git cat-file --batch-check` for every distinct readable blob and keeps the map. It never checks `entryLimit` first. The bound the store's base decision relies on is "Memory for the entries: 65,536 entries, `entryLimit`, checked before any size is read" and "Memory for the sizes: one line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it". The new call bounds those resources only by listing bytes. 64 MiB is a KiB a line only on average: a short record path makes a line about 78 bytes.
explanation.whatToDo: Count `listing.entries.length` against `entryLimit` before calling `#sizes`. Past the limit, return the entry count and listing bytes with record bytes marked as not counted, as `unlisted` already does for the listing. Or cap the sizes request some other way, and record the bound in the decision's table.
explanation.whyHere: `size()` is built to answer on a tip past a limit, and that is the case where this matters. Doctor, `melian records size` and the round's `size` job all call it on exactly such a tip. The memory and the cat-file input and output that `entryLimit` existed to cap now grow to about 13 times the limit. The change also adds no row to the decision's resource table, though the state-git guideline says a new resource a call takes must go there with its bound.

properties.failureScenario: A writer on an older build, or a push by hand (both of which the base decision says can leave a tip past a limit), leaves `melian/state` holding about 860,000 distinct records at paths like `changesets/x/y/z/a.json`. That is 78 bytes per `ls-tree -r -z` line, about 64 MiB in total, so it stays within `listingLimit`. Every read refuses this tip at `#measure`'s `entries.length > entryLimit` check, before any size is read. `melian doctor`, `melian records size` and the round's `size` job then call `GitRecordStore.size()`, and from there `StateTree.size`. That call keeps all ~860,000 `TreeEntry` objects, builds a Set of 860,000 oids, and pipes about 35 MB of oids into `cat-file --batch-check`. It reads back about 45 MB of output through `#succeed`, which has no output bound, and builds an 860,000-entry Map. That is roughly 13 times the 65,536-entry bound the decision promises for entries and sizes. The result is heavy memory use, and time spent up to the deadline, in doctor and in the size job. The size job's 2-minute step timeout can end the read, so the comment says the size could not be read on the very tip the warning exists for.
